title: McDonald's pulled the Quarter Pounder in 1 in 5 US restaurants and traced the E. coli to one onion plant
description: In 2024 an E. coli outbreak was linked to the Quarter Pounder. Shows how it was traced to one onion plant, and how wide to pull a product before the cause is known.
caption: US McDonald's restaurants pulled the Quarter Pounder

title: How Delta, United and American recovered from the CrowdStrike outage
description: In July 2024 a faulty software update crashed Windows computers and grounded US airlines. Follows the week day by day: what Delta, United and American did, and why Delta needed five days to fly normally again.
caption: for Delta to fly normally again, when United took 3 and American 1

title: The power tower that stopped a gigafactory
description: In 2024 a fire under one power line cut Tesla's Berlin plant off the grid for eight days. Covers what it cost and what the plant could have done instead.
caption: off the grid after a fire under one power line

title: Adidas was stuck with €1.2 billion of Yeezy shoes and sold every pair
description: In 2022 Adidas ended its Yeezy deal with €1.2 billion of shoes in stock. Compares burning, keeping and selling them, and how fast to sell.
caption: of Yeezy shoes stuck in its warehouses

title: One ship, sideways, and 422 ships waiting
description: In 2021 a container ship blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Covers the choice to wait or sail around Africa, and the rush at Europe's ports afterwards.
caption: ships waiting while the Ever Given blocked the canal

title: Peloton built for a boom that ended
description: In 2020 Peloton could not make bikes fast enough. It added factories and stock, then demand fell. Shows the question it faced, what it decided, and the cost of building for a spike.
caption: lost in one year after building for a boom that ended

title: Why Zara kept its factories close to home
description: In the 1990s rivals moved their sewing to Asia. Zara asked whether to make clothes where it was cheapest or fastest, kept trend items close to home, and cut its sales and leftovers.
caption: from first sketch to store, when rivals took 5 to 6 months

title: First cross-dock ever: Berlin Airlift ’48
description: In 1948 the Soviets cut every road into West Berlin. Shows how the Allies supplied 2 million people by air, and how fixed landing slots and short ground times turned the airports into a fast cross-dock.
caption: between landings, day and night, to supply 2 million people

title: Supply allocation models, explained
description: One week on a chip maker's allocation desk: 100 chips, 160 ordered. Each day brings a new problem, fixed by a different allocation model, from rationing and quotas to fairness rules and auctions.
caption: 160 chips ordered, 100 in stock. Who gets them?
